en: The Laghukaumudī Grammar.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Having bowed to the goddess Sarasvatī, who is pure and possessed of all virtues, I compose this *Laghusiddhāntakaumudī* for the purpose of entering the system of Pāṇini.
The Laghukaumudī Grammar.

Thus it is: for each of these phonemes—a, i, u, and ṛ—there are eighteen varieties.

There are twelve [sounds] for the *lṛ*-vowel because it lacks a long form; there are also twelve for the *eC* vowels because they lack short forms. "That which has the same place of articulation and effort is homogeneous (*savarṇa*). (Pāṇini 1.1.9)

That which has the same pair of [factors]—the internal place of articulation (*sthāna*) such as the palate and the internal effort (*ābhyantara-prayatna*)—is designated as *savarṇa* (homogeneous) with respect to one another.

It should be stated that there is mutual homogeneity (*sāvarṇya*) between the vowels *ṛ* and *ḷ*. (4) The throat is the [place of articulation] for *a*, *ku* (the velars), and the visarga (*visarjanīya*).
The palate is the place of articulation for *icuyaśāḥ*;
the head for *ṛṭuraṣāḥ*;
and the teeth for *lṛtulasāḥ*.
For the *upadhmānīya* and *upū* sounds, the lips are the articulator;
for *ñ*, *ma*, *ṅ*, *ṇ*, and *na*, the nose as well;
for *e* and *o*, the throat and palate.
The *odaut* vowels are articulated with the throat and lips;
the letter *va* is articulated with the teeth and lips;
and the *jihvāmūlīya* is articulated at the root of the tongue.
Regarding the anusvāra of the nose:

The first [type of articulation] is fivefold, due to the distinctions of *spṛṣṭa* (contact), *īṣatspṛṣṭa* (slight contact), *īṣadvivṛta* (slightly open), *vivṛta* (open), and *saṃvṛta* (closed). Among these, the effort (*prayatna*) of contact belongs to the *sparśa* (stop) consonants.
The semi-vowels (*antasthā*) are slightly touched;
the sibilants (*ūṣman*) are slightly opened;
the vowels (*svara*) are fully opened.
When a short *a*-vowel is employed, it is closed (*saṃvṛta*);
however, during the stage of grammatical derivation (*prakriyā*), it is indeed open (*vivṛta*).
Externally, however, [the articulation] is of eleven kinds.

Expansion (*vivāra*), contraction (*saṃvāra*), breath (*śvāsa*), resonance (*nāda*), voiced (*ghoṣa*), unvoiced (*aghoṣa*), weak-aspirated (*alpaprāṇa*), strong-aspirated (*mahāprāṇa*), acute (*udātta*), grave (*anudātta*), and circumflex (*svarita*). The *khara* [consonants] are characterized by expansion, breath, and are unvoiced. (5) The *haś* [consonants] are characterized by contraction, resonance, and are voiced.

The first, third, and fifth letters of the classes (*varga*), as well as the *yaṇ* sounds, are of small breath (*alpa-prāṇa*). The second and fourth letters of the classes, along with the *śala* sounds, are of great breath (*mahā-prāṇa*). The consonants beginning with *ka* and ending with *ma* are the stops (*sparśa*).
The *yaṇ* sounds are the semivowels (*antaḥstha*).
The *śal* sounds are the sibilants and aspirates (*ūṣman*). The vowels (*ac*) are the tones (*svara*).
The *jihvāmūlīya* is like a half-*visarga* occurring before *ka* and *kha*, [arising] from *ka* and *kha*.
The *upadhmānīya* is like a half-*visarga* occurring before *pa* and *pha*, [arising] from *pa* and *pha*.
The *anusvāra* and *visarga* occur after the vowels *aṃ* and *aḥ*, respectively.

the Vatsas. (355) But when an ancestor is living, the term *yuvan* [is used for the descendant]. Pāṇini 4.1.163.

When an ancestor such as a father or grandfather is living, the offspring of a grandson or later descendant—beginning with the fourth generation—shall bear the designation *yuvan* (youth) alone. *Gotrād yūni stryām* (Pāṇini 4.1.94): In the case of a youth-descendant, the suffix shall be applied only after a suffix denoting the *gotra* (clan); however, in the feminine gender, the designation *yuvan* does not apply.

4.1.94: *gotrād yūni striyām* | A suffix [denoting a descendant] should be applied only after a word ending in a *gotra*-suffix to denote a young descendant (*yuvan*), but in the case of a female, there is no designation as *yuvan*.
4.1.101: *yañiñoś ca* | [The suffix *phak* is applied] after [stems ending in] *yañ* and *iñ*.
The suffix *phak* is applied after a word ending in *yañ* or *iñ* when it denotes lineage (*gotra*).

[Pāṇini 4.1.95] Regarding the rule *āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhacchaghāṃ pratyayādīnām* [Pāṇini 7.1.2]: for the initial sounds of suffixes, *pha* becomes *āyan*, *ḍha* becomes *ey*, *kha* becomes *īn*, *cha* becomes *īy*, and *gha* becomes *iy*.
The young descendant of Garga is Gārgyāyaṇa; [likewise] Dākṣāyaṇa.
(356) *ata iñ* 4.1.95. [The suffix *iñ* is applied after a stem ending in short *a* to form patronymics.]
In the sense of "offspring": *dākṣiḥ*.
[The suffix *iñ* is applied after the class of stems beginning with *bāhu*: 4.1.96.]
Bāhavi; Auḍulomi. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class).

The suffix *añ* is applied after [names] such as *vid* to form patronymics from those who are not *ṛṣis*, provided they do not follow an *ānantarya* (immediate) relationship; otherwise, it is used for the *gotra*. The *gotra* descendant of *Vida* is *Vaida*.
Vaidau.
The offspring of Vidā’s son is a grandson (pautraḥ). [Nominative dual:
Pautrau.

The suffix *pautra* (grandson) is formed in this same manner; likewise for *dauhitra* (daughter's son) and others. [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied after [the group of words beginning with] *śiva*. (Pāṇini 4.1.112)
(357) Regarding offspring: *śaivaḥ* (a son of Śiva),
*gāṅgaḥ* (a son of Gaṅgā).
[The suffix *cha* is applied] after [words denoting] sages (*ṛṣi*), Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis, and Kurus. 4.1.114. After sages:
Vāsiṣṭha.
Vaiśvāmitra [received it] from the Andhakas;
Śvāphalka [received it] from them.
From the Vṛṣṇis,
Vāsudeva;
from the Kurus.
The suffix *nā* is applied after the name of a mother whose name begins with *utsaṅkhyā* or *saṃbhadrā*, [to form a patronymic]. (Pāṇini 4.1.115)
For the word *mātṛ* preceded by a numeral and so forth, there shall be the substitution of *ud* and the suffix *aṇ*. Examples: *dvaimāturaḥ*, *ṣāṇmāturaḥ*.
Sāṃmāturaḥ;
Bhādramāturaḥ. [The suffix] Ḍhak [is applied after feminine stems] to form patronymics. 4.1.120.
The suffix *ḍhak* is applied after words ending in feminine suffixes; for example, *vainateyaḥ*.
(358) [Vārttika: For the word *kanyā*, the substitute *kanīna* is also applied [before the suffix *ḍhak*]; 4.1.116.
And [the suffix] *aṇ*. Vyāsa is the son of Kānīna, as is Karṇa.
[The suffix] *yat* is applied after words such as *rājan* and *śvaśura*. 4.1.137.

In the case of *rājan*, [the penultimate vowel remains unchanged] only when [a suffix beginning with *ya* follows] that denotes the agent (*kartṛ*). And those [suffixes] which denote neither the action (*bhāva*) nor the object (*karman*): 6.4.168.
When a *taddhita* suffix beginning with *ya* follows, the base form (*prakṛti*) shall remain as it is, except in the case of [suffixes] denoting the action or the object.
*rājanyaḥ* [is formed by *yañ*] when denoting a genus (*jāti*). Why [is it said] "only when denoting a genus"? [To exclude: *rājana*. 6.4.167.
The suffixes *añ* and *ṣyañ* are applied after [stems ending in] *prakṛti*, *rājan*, and *śvaśura*. *prākṛtaḥ*, *rājanyaḥ*, *śvāśuryaḥ*.
(359) *kṣatrād dhaḥ* | 4 | 1 | 138 | [The suffix] *dha* is applied after *kṣatra*. [The resulting form is] *kṣatriyaḥ*. Only when referring to a genus (*jāti*) is this rule applicable.
*kṣātra* is another [derivative].
[The suffix] *ṭhak* is applied after [stems ending in] *revatī* and others (Pāṇini 4.1.146).
[In the case of a suffix beginning with] *ṭha*, *ika* is substituted for it (Pāṇini 7.3.50).
The single substitute *ik* is applied in place of the *ṭha* that follows a stem-final vowel.
*Raivatikaḥ*.
[From a word denoting a country, the suffix *añ* is applied after a word denoting a Kṣatriya. 4.1.168.
The suffix *añ* is applied after a word denoting a country (*janapada*) that also denotes a *kṣatriya*, when forming a patronymic (*apatya*). For example: *pāñcālaḥ*.
After a country name that shares its name with a *kṣatriya*, the suffix is applied as it would be for the descendant of a king.
The king of the Pañcālas is Pāñcāla; [the descendant] of Puru is Paurava.
(360) After *pāṇḍu*, the suffix *ḍyañ* is applied.
*Pāṇḍyaḥ*.
After *kuru*, *nādi*, and others, the suffix *ṇya* is applied [to form patronymics]. Pāṇini 4.1.172.

*Kauravyaḥ* (a descendant of Kuru), *naiṣadhyaḥ* (a descendant of Niṣadha): these are formed by the suffix *yañ* [added to the names of tribes] when they denote the king of that tribe. Pāṇini 4.1.174.

The suffixes *añ* and so forth shall bear the technical designation *tadrāja*. Pāṇini 2.4.62: When many [descendants] are denoted, the *tadrāja* suffix is elided by that very same rule, provided it does not refer to a feminine. When a plurality of objects is expressed, there is elision (*luk*) of the *tadrāja* suffix when that plurality is caused by those very [descendants], but not in the feminine.
The Pañcālas, and so forth. [From this point] *luk* [is substituted for the suffix] after *kamboja*. Pāṇini 4.1.175.
From this [rule], there is elision (*luk*) of the *tadrāja* suffix.
*Kambojaḥ*, *kambojau*.
It should be stated that [the suffix applies] after *kamboja* and others:
*colaḥ*, *śakaḥ*.
*Keralaḥ* | *Yavanaḥ* | (361) Thus ends the section on offspring (*apatya*).

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied [after a word denoting the substance with which something is dyed] in the sense of "dyed by that" (*rāgāt*). A garment dyed with a decoction (*kaṣāya*) is called *kāṣāya*.
Time conjoined with a lunar mansion [takes the suffix] *aṇ*. [Pāṇini 4.2.3]. The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied.
It should be stated that in the case of *tiṣya* and *puṣya*, when they denote lunar mansions, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the *y*.

The *pauṣamahaḥ* (the festival of the month of Pauṣa) is that which is joined with the Puṣya [nakṣatra]. Regarding the elision (*lup*) without distinction: Pāṇini 4.2.4 states that there is elision (*lup*) of the suffix prescribed by the preceding rule when no specific internal division of time consisting of sixty *daṇḍas* is understood.
Today is the Puṣya [asterism].
(362) The Sāman has been seen. 4.2.7. By that very [means].
The *sāman* seen by Vasiṣṭha is the *vāsiṣṭha*. [By the rule] "From Vāmadeva, the suffixes ḍya and ḍya," the *sāman* seen by Vāmadeva is the *vāmadevya*.
*Parivṛto rathaḥ* (4.2.10): In this sense, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.
A chariot covered with cloth is a *vāstra* chariot.

In that context, [the suffix ṭhañ is used] after words meaning "vessels" when they denote what has been taken out [from them]. (4.2.14) For example: *śārāva odanaḥ* ("rice taken out in a shallow dish").
[The suffix ṭhañ is used] after a word meaning "prepared" when it denotes edible food. (4.2.16)

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after a word ending in the seventh case when the sense is "prepared," provided that what is prepared consists of edible foods. For example, foods prepared in frying pans (*bhrāṣṭra*) are called *bhrāṣṭrāḥ*. (363) [The suffix *aṇ* is also applied] in the sense of "this has as its deity" (*sā'sya devatā*). Pāṇini 4.2.24.
That which has Indra as its deity is the *aindra* oblation;
the *pāśupata*; the *bārhaspatya*.
After *śukra*, the suffix *dhak* [is applied] (Pāṇini 4.2.26):
*śaukriya*. After *soma*, the suffix *ṭyaṇ* [is applied] (Pāṇini 4.2.30).
[The suffix *yañ* is applied] after [the word *saumya*];
and after [words ending in] *vāyu*, *ṛtu*, *pitṛ*, and *uṣas*, [the suffix *yañ* is applied]. 4.2.31.
*Vāyavya*.
Regarding the term *ṛtavya*:
"rīṅ is substituted for ṛ" (Pāṇini 7.4.27).
When an affix beginning with *y* that is not a *kṛt* suffix follows, as well as when the *yak* of the present stem (*sārvadhātuka*) or the *cvī* suffix follow, *rīṅ* is the substitute for *ṛ*.
And [the word] "yasya" [is used].
[The examples are] "pitryam" and "uṣasyam".
(364) *pitṛvya-mātula-mātāmaha-pitāmahāḥ* 4 | 2 | 36. These are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*). The brother of one's father is *pitṛvyaḥ*.
The mother’s brother is the maternal uncle (mātula).
The mother’s father is the maternal grandfather (mātāmaha).
The father’s father is the paternal grandfather (pitāmaha).
"Denoting a collection thereof" (tasya samūhaḥ) [is the sense of the suffixes taught hereafter]. (Pāṇini 4.2.37). A collection of crows is a *kāka* (crow-flock).
[The suffix] *aṇ* is applied after words such as *bhikṣā*. (Pāṇini 4.2.38).
Alms.
A collection of pregnant women is *gārbhiṇam*.
Here, since the suffix belongs to the *aḍha* group, the masculine form is applied according to the rule for *puṃvadbhāva*.

*inaṇyanapatye* (Pāṇini 6.4.164): When the suffix *aṇ* is used in a sense other than "offspring," the stem ending in *in* remains in its original form (*prakṛti*). Consequently, by the rule *tena nastaddhite*, the elision of the final vowel and following consonant (*ṭilopa*) does not occur.
A collection of young women is *yauvatam*. (365) By the rule *grāma-jana-bandhubhyas-tal* (Pāṇini 4.2.43), a word ending in *tal* is feminine.
The state of being a village; the state of being a populace; the state of being a kinsman.
And it should be stated that [the suffix -tva] is applied after the words *gaja* and *sahāya*: *gajatā*,
*sahāyatā*.
The suffix *kha* is applied after the word *ahan* when it refers to a sacrificial rite (*kratu*). [Thus:
*ahīna*. The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after the words *acitta*, *hastin*, and *dhenu*. 4.2.47.
*Isusuktāntāt kaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.51): After a word ending in *i*, *u*, or a suffix marked with *k* (*uk*), the suffix *ṭha* is replaced by *ka*. For example: *sāktukam*.
*hāstikam* (a herd of elephants), *dhainukam* (a herd of milch-cows).
[The suffix *ṭhak* is added after these words] when meaning "one who studies that" or "one who knows that. (Pāṇini 4.2.59)

(366) *Na yvābhyāṃ padāntābhyāṃ pūrvas tu tābhyām aic* | 7 | 3 | 3 | Vṛddhi is not substituted for a vowel following *y* or *v* at the end of a word; rather, the augments *ai* and *au* respectively are inserted before those two. For example: one who studies or knows grammar is called a *vaiyākaraṇaḥ*.
The suffix *vun* is applied after *krama*, etc., [to form agent nouns]. Examples:
*kramakaḥ*, *padakaḥ*.
Śikṣaka (teacher), mīmāṃsaka (investigator). [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] to denote that something exists in this place, when the name of that place is used [as the base]. 4.2.67.
The *udumbara* trees exist in this region; thus, it is called the "Audumbara" region. [Pāṇini 4.2.68] A city established by Kuśāmba is *Kauśāmbī*.
(367) "The place of residence of that [people]" [is formed by adding the suffix *aṇ*]. 4.2.69.
The country which is the residence of the Śivīs is called *śaiva*. Also [the suffix is added] for that which is situated not far from [a place]. 4.2.70.
Vaidiśa is that which is not far from Vidiśā.
[Pāṇini 1.2.51:
When a country (janapada) is to be expressed, there is elision (lup) of the secondary suffixes (cāturarthika) [denoting the four senses].

When *lup* occurs, the gender and number remain as those of the base (*prakṛti*). When *lup* is applied, the gender and number are like those of the original form. For example: "The country which is the dwelling place of the Pañcālas" is called *pañcālāḥ*.
The Kurus;
the Aṅgas;
the Vaṅgas.
*Kaliṅgāḥ*.
[The suffix] *añ* is applied after [the word] *varaṇa* and others. Rule 4.2.82: This rule is commenced because the meaning of the base word (*padārtha*) is not [already] covered by the previous rule.
The city situated not far from the Varaṇā [river] is called Varaṇāḥ.
(368) [The suffix] *ḍmatup* is applied after the words *kumuda*, *naḍa*, and *vetasa*. [The suffix] is applied after a word ending in a *jhay* [consonant]. 8.2.10. 4.2.87.
After a word ending in a *jh* sound, the *m* of the suffix *matup* is optionally replaced by *v*.
Examples: *kumudvān*, *naḍvān*.
After a word ending in *m* or *v*, or having *m* or *v* as its penultimate (*upadhā*) letter, provided it is not one of the *yava*-group, the *m* of the suffix *mat* is replaced by *v*. Example:
*vetasvān*.

The suffix *valac* is applied after *naḍa* and *śāda*. (Pāṇini 4.2.88) — *naḍvalaḥ* ("a place abounding in reeds"). The suffix *valac* is applied after *śikhā*. (Pāṇini 4.2.89) — *śikhāvalaḥ* ("possessing a crest").
Śikhāvalaḥ. These are the [words] formed with the suffixes having four meanings (cāturarthika).

*Śeṣe* | 4 | 2 | 92 | (369) "The remainder" (*śeṣa*) refers to any meaning other than those beginning with "offspring" (*apatya*) and ending with the fourfold sense (*caturarthī*). In that case, the suffixes *aṇ* and others shall apply. For example: that which is perceived by the eye is *cākṣuṣaṃ rūpam* ("visual form").
Sound is heard by the ear (*śrāvaṇa*). The person is known from the Upaniṣads (*aupaniṣada*). Flour ground on a grinding stone is *dārṣada*.
A four-borne cart is called *cāturaṃ* [shakaṭam].
On the fourteenth day, the fourteenth-night demon (*cāturdaśaṃ rakṣaḥ*) is seen.
From this point until the section on "modification" (*vikāra*), the remainder of the rules apply.
The suffixes *dhak* and *kha* are added [to the word *rāṣṭra*] after *rāṣṭra* and *avārapāra* [in the sense of "born in" and so forth].
4.2.93. *Rāṣṭriyaḥ* ("one born in a kingdom") from *rāṣṭra*; *avārapārīṇaḥ* ("one who has gone from this shore to the other").
It should also be stated that [the suffix -īna] occurs after *avāra* and *pāra* when they are compounded with *vi* and *gṛhīta*, and even when they are reversed:
*avārīṇaḥ* and *pārīṇaḥ*.
*Pārāvarīṇaḥ*.

Here, due to the specific nature of the context, suffixes beginning with *gha* and ending with *ṭya*, *uṭ*, and *lyuṭ* are mentioned; their specific meanings, such as "born there" (*jāta*), and their governing case-endings (*samartha-vibhakti*) will now be stated.
(370) *grāmādyakhañau* | 4 | 2 | 94 | [The suffixes] *ya* and *khañ* are applied after the word *grāma*. (4.2.94)
*grāmyaḥ* (rustic); *grāmīṇaḥ* (villager).
[The suffix] *ḍhak* is added after words such as *nadī* (river) [to denote "born there" or "belonging there"]. Pāṇini 4.2.97.
It is from Nādeya; it is from Moheya; it is from Vārāṇasī.
The suffix *tyak* is applied after [the words] *dakṣiṇa*, *apaśca*, and *puras*. (Pāṇini 4.2.98) *dākṣiṇātyaḥ* (southern);
*pāścāttyaḥ* (western).
[The suffix] *yat* is applied after [the word] *paurastya*.
[Pāṇini 4.2.101 states: "After *dyu*, *prāk*, *apāk*, *udak*, and *pratīc*, [the suffix] *yat* [is applied].
[Thus we have] *divyam*.
Eastern; southern; northern.
[The suffix] *tyap* is added after an indeclinable [denoting direction]. (Pāṇini 4.2.104) [This applies] only after *ama*, *iha*, *kutaḥ*, *tataḥ*, *sita*, and *trebhiḥ*.
A minister;
one belonging to this place;
one belonging to that place.
*tatastyaḥ* and *tatratyaḥ*. [The suffix] *tyap* is applied after *tatas* and *tatra* when denoting something fixed (*dhruve*).
[The term] *nitya* [is established].
"That whose first vowel among its vowels is *vṛddhi* is called *vṛddha*" (Pāṇini 1.1.73).
That aggregate (*samudāya*) among whose vowels the first is a *vṛddhi* vowel shall receive the designation *vṛddha*.
And the words beginning with *tyad* (P.
1.1.74) shall have the designation *vṛddha*.
From a *vṛddha* [stem], the suffix *cha* is applied (P. 4.2.114).
The suffix *cha* (forming *śālīya*) or *cha* (forming *tadīya*) may optionally be applied after a name.
The designation of seniority:
*devadattīyaḥ*, *daivadattaḥ*.

(372) Pāṇini 4.2.138: *gahādibhyaśca* (and after *gaha* and others). [The suffix *cha* is applied]. Example: *gahīyaḥ*. Pāṇini 4.3.1: *yuṣmadasmadoranyatarasyāṃ khañ ca* (and optionally *khañ* after *yuṣmad* and *asmad*). [The suffixes *cha* and *khañ* are applied].
The suffix *cha* is applied;
alternatively, the suffix *aṇ*.
Thus, "belonging to you two" or "belonging to you all" is *yuṣmadīyaḥ*.
"Belonging to us.

[In the rule] "In that [context], *yuṣmāka* and *asmāka* [are substituted] for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* when followed by *aṇ* and *khañ*" (Pāṇini 4.3.2), these two substitutions (*yuṣmāka* and *asmāka*) occur for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* when *khañ* or *aṇ* follows.
yauṣmākīṇaḥ (belonging to you),
āsmākīnaḥ (belonging to us),
yauṣmākaḥ (belonging to you).

*Āsmākaḥ*. *Tavaka-mamaka-ekavacane* (Pāṇini 4.3.3): When expressing a single referent, the substitutes *tavaka* and *mamaka* take the place of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* respectively before the suffixes *khañ* and *aṇ*.
tāvakīnaḥ, tāvakaḥ, māmakīnaḥ.
*māmaka-* [is substituted for *mad*] when followed by the suffix *-cha* or when it occurs as the final member of a compound. 7.2.98.

(373) For these two [pronouns], *tvad* and *mad*, which denote a single referent and are not limited [in number], the substitutes *tvam* and *mam* occur when a suffix or a subsequent member (*uttarapada*) follows.
*Tvadīyaḥ*; *madīyaḥ*.
*tvatputraḥ* (your son), *matputraḥ* (my son); [the substitution of] *ma* for [the genitive suffix] *ṅasi* after *madhya-*; Pāṇini 4.3.8.
The suffix *madhyama* [is used after a word denoting time]. 4.3.11: *kāla* + *ṭhañ* = *kālikam*.
Monthly; annual. There is elision of the suffix *ṭi* after indeclinables when followed by a mere case-ending.
The suffix *ṭhañ* (forming *īna*) is applied after the words *sāyaṃprātaḥ*,
*paunaḥpunya*, and *prāvṛṣ* to form derivatives meaning "belonging to" or "occurring at" those times. (Pāṇini 4.3.17)
*Prāvṛṣeṇyaḥ*.

[The suffixes] *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* are added after the indeclinables *sāyaṃ*, *ciraṃ*, *prāhṇe*, and *prage*, and the augment *tuṭ* is also added. (Pāṇini 4.3.23) After these four indeclinables and other words denoting time, the suffixes *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* occur, and the augment *tuṭ* is applied to them.
*sāyaṃtanam* (belonging to evening);
*ciraṃtanam* (ancient).
In these two words, the elision of the final vowel and consonant (*at-antatvam*) is prescribed for the forms *prāhṇe* and *prage*.
prāhṇetana, pragetana,
doṣātanam.
*tatra jātaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.3.25): After a word ending in the seventh case, the suffixes *aṇ* and others, as well as *gha* and others, are applied in the sense of "born there. Example:
*srughne jātaḥ* ("born in Srughna").
Sraughnaḥ;
born in Utse,
Autsaḥ.
Born in the kingdom: *rāṣṭriya*. Born on this side or the other shore: *avārapāre jātaḥ*.
"Avārapārīṇaḥ" and so forth. [The suffix] ṭhap [is applied] after "prāvṛṣ". Pāṇini 4.3.26.
The suffix *cha* (forming *eya*) is applied after the words *eṇī*,
*prāvṛṣ*, and *prāya* [to denote "born there" or "produced there"]. 4.3.39.
(375) It is exactly as follows: one who generally or predominantly resides in Srughna is called *sraughna*.
[The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after the word *saṃbhūta* [in the sense of "become"]. 4.3.41.
One who is born in Srughna is a *sraughna*. [The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after *kośala*. 4.3.42.
*Kauśeya* means silk cloth. [The suffix *aṇ*] is applied in the sense of "originating therefrom" (4.3.53): *sraughnaḥ*, *autsaḥ*.
*rāṣṭriyaḥ* (belonging to the kingdom).
[The suffix] *yat* is applied after words such as *diś* (direction) and others.
*Diśyam* (pertaining to the direction).
[The suffix *yañ* is applied after a word denoting a member of a class. From [the rule] "And after a part of the body" (Pāṇini 4.3.55): *dantyam*.
This is clear from the context. The suffix *iṣṭhan* is desired after the word *adhyātma* and others.
That which exists within the self (*adhyātman*) is *ādhyātmika*.
(376) And for the *anuśatika*-class [of words], 7.3.20:
in these, there is vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of both members of the compound before an affix marked with Ñ or Ṇ, or one that is K. Example:
*ādhidaivikam*.
Pertaining to living beings (ādhibhautika);
pertaining to this world (aihalaukika);
this is an open-ended class (ākṛtigaṇa).
The letter *cha* is substituted for the jihvāmūlīya and the aṅguliya.
(Pāṇini 4.3.62) Jihvāmūlīya;
aṅguliya.
[The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in a consonant of the *ka*-group. [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] in the sense of "come from that. 4.3.63;
"He has come from Srughna" (*srughnād āgataḥ*). "A resident of Srughna" (*sraughnaḥ*). (377) *ṭhak* [is applied] after words denoting places where officials reside. Pāṇini 4.3.75.
One who has come from the customs house is a *śaulkaśālika*. [The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after words denoting a connection through learning or birth. (Pāṇini 4.3.77) For example: *aupādhyāyakaḥ*.
*paitāmahakaḥ* (belonging to the grandfather).
The suffix *rūpya-* optionally occurs after words expressing a cause (*hetu*) and after words denoting humans (*manuṣya*).

In the sense of "belonging to" (pakṣe), the suffix *cha* is applied because [the word] belongs to the *gahādi* group:

*devadattarūpyam*.
The suffix *mayaṭ* is also applied [to denote "made of" or "consisting of"]. (Pāṇini 4.3.82) Example:
*samamayam*.
The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied [to indicate origin]. 4.3.83. The Gaṅgā originates from the Himavat; thus, she is called *haimavatī*.

"Proclaimed by him": 4.3.101.

"Belonging to that": 4.3.120.
"Aupagava" [means] "this belongs to Upagu"; thus end the secondary derivatives (*śaiṣika*).
(379) *tasya vikāraḥ* | 4 | 3 | 134 | In the sense of a modification (*vikāra*) of stone (*aśman*), there is the elision of the *ṭi* suffix. A modification of stone is *āśma*.

*gomayaṃ* (cow-dung).

*dādhika* means "prepared with curd. [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after a word denoting a substance] when it is mixed [with another substance]. 4.4.22. That which is mixed with curd is *dādhika*.
[The suffix *ṭhan* is added after a word ending in the sixth case] when the sense is "he gathers by gleaning. (4.4.32) He gathers jujube fruits; thus, he is a *bādarika*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* is added] when the sense is "he protects. (4.4.33)
One who protects the community is a *sāmājika*.

One who makes a drum is a *dārdurika*.
One who practices the Dharma is *dharmika* (Pāṇini 4.4.41).
And it should be stated [that the suffix *cha* is added] after the word *adharma*.
[The derivative form is] *ādharmika*. [The suffix *cha* is added after] *śilpa*. 4.4.55.

*Praharaṇa* (Pāṇini 4.4.57): [The suffix *ṭhak* is added after a word denoting a weapon].

One whose habit (*śīla*) is eating cakes (*apūpa-bhakṣaṇa*) is called *āpūpika*.
(383) *nikaṭe vasati* | 4 | 4 | 73 | "A monk who dwells nearby is a *naikaṭika*. Thus ends the section on the suffix *ṭhak*.

The suffix *yat* is introduced from here up to [the rule] 4.4.75, *prāgdhitāt*. [The suffix *ya* is introduced after a word ending in the second case to form a compound meaning] "it carries that": *tadvahati rathayugaprāsaṅgam* (4.4.76).

[The suffix *ya* is applied after the words] *nau*, *vayas*, *dharma*, *viṣa*, *mūla-mūla*, *sītā*, *tulā*, and [the words ending in] *tulya*, *prāpya*, *vadha*, *ānamya*, *sama*, and *samita*. 4|4|91.

Thus, this is the limit.

"Belonging to the Mothers.

From these [suffixes],

*vadhyaḥ* (meaning "to be killed") [is used as a suffix]. 5.1.79: *tena nirvṛttam* ("accomplished by means of that"). *ahnā nirvṛttam āhnikam* ("that which is accomplished by means of a day is 'daily'").
Thus ends the limit for the suffix *ṭhañ*.
The suffix *vati* is used when there is an action equal to that [of another], according to Pāṇini 5.1.115: *tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ*. For example:
*brāhmaṇena tulyaṃ brāhmaṇavad adhīte* ("He studies like a Brāhmaṇa"). Why specify "if it is an action"? [Because the suffix is not used for equality in non-action].

For example: "sthūlaḥ putreṇa tulyaḥ" ("He is as fat as his son"). (388) *tatra tasyeva* (5.1.116).

As in "mathurāyām iva" (as in Mathurā), [the suffix *vat* is used] as in "mathurāvat srughne prākāraḥ" (there is a wall in Srughna as in Mathurā); as in "caitrasya iva" (like Caitra's), [the suffix *vat* is used] as in "caitravan maitrasya gāvaḥ" (Maitra’s cows are like Caitra’s).
The suffixes *tva* and *tal* are used in the sense of "the state of that" (*tasya bhāvaḥ*). Pāṇini 5.1.119.
In a cognition produced by a *prakṛti*, that which serves as the qualifier (*prakāra*) is the abstract state (*bhāva*). For example, the abstract state of a cow is "cowness" (*gotva*).
A word ending in the suffix *-tva* is neuter.

The particle *ca* (and) is for the purpose of including [the suffixes] *nañ* and *snañ* as well. The state of being a woman (*strī*) is *straiṇa* or *strītva*.
Femininity; masculinity; manhood.
Masculinity. (389) *pṛthv-ādibhya imanij vā* (Pāṇini 5.1.122).

mradimā; mārdavam.

Whiteness;
firmness; solidity.

After the words *dvi* and *tri*, the suffix *taya* takes the augment *ayac*. Thus: *dvayam* (a pair) and *tritayam* (a triad).

The sixth (*ṣaṣṭha*) is that which completes six; it is the ordinal [number]. [Regarding] *katitha*:

This is an exception to the suffix *ḍaṭ*.

[The suffix *ḍaṭ* is applied after the word *dvi* to form] *dvitīya*, meaning "the second" (one who completes two). [After the word *tri*, the suffix *ḍaṭ* is applied] and there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the vowel. (Pāṇini 5.2.55)
(394) Third [sūtra]:

5.2.87: [The suffix *ini* is applied] also after a word ending in *pūrva*. Example: *kṛtapūrvī* (one who has previously performed).
5.2.88: [The suffix *ini* is applied] also after words such as *iṣṭa*.
The suffix *iṣṭhan* is applied after a word ending in *iṣṭa* [to form a superlative], as in *iṣṭī*. The suffix *adhītī* is formed with *iṣṭhan*.
The suffix *matup* is applied in the sense of "this belongs to him" (*tad asyāsti*) or "this is in this" (*tasmin asti*). (Pāṇini 5.2.94)
One who has cows in this [place] or for whom they exist is "gomān" (possessing cows).
(395) *tasau matvarthe* | 1 | 4 | 19 | A stem ending in *-ta* or *-sa* receives the designation *bha* when followed by an affix expressing possession (*matvartha*).

*cūḍālaḥ* (one who has a crest); *cūḍāvān* (one who possesses a crest). Why [is it specified] "situated on a living being"? [To exclude cases such as: *vṛkṣaś cūḍāvān*.

*pāmanaḥ* (one suffering from scabies);

Famous;
renowned;

[formed] by *ac* after *arśas-* etc., according to Pāṇini 5.2.127; [thus] *arśasaḥ* (one who has hemorrhoids).

5.3.1. *prāg-diśo vibhaktiḥ*. The suffixes to be mentioned hereafter, prior to [the rule concerning] words denoting direction (*dik-śabda*), shall bear the technical designation *vibhakti* (case-ending).
Now, the suffixes having their own meaning (*svārthika*).
"From *kim*, all pronouns (*sarvanāman*), and *bahu*, except for *dvi* and so forth" (Pāṇini 5.3.2).
This prescribes that [the suffix] follows *kim*, all pronouns, and the word *bahu*, as an extension of the heading "before the case-endings of the directions" (*prāgdiśaḥ*).

*tasil* [is the suffix] after the fifth case (pañcamī). (Pāṇini 5.3.7) The suffix *tasil* may optionally occur after words such as *kim* when they end in the fifth case. *ku* [is substituted for *kim*] before *ti* and *hu*. (Pāṇini 7.2.104)
(399) For the word *kimaḥ*, the substitute *ku* is applied before case endings beginning with *t* or *h*. Thus:
*kutaḥ* (from where), *kasmāt* (from which).
The suffix *idam* [becomes *ita*] before a *prāgdiśīya* [suffix]. Example: *itaḥ*.
*etado 'n* (Pāṇini 5.3.5):
[The substitute *an* is applied] in the sense of the *prāgdiśīya* suffixes. Because it consists of more than one phoneme (*anekāl*), it replaces the whole [of the original base].
From here; from there; from which.
Then: from many; but from two or more.
The suffix *tasil* is applied after the two [words] *pary-ā* and *abhi*. (Pāṇini 5.3.9)
*Paritaḥ*:
meaning "on all sides. *Abhitaḥ*.
The meaning is "on both sides. [The suffix] *traL* is applied after a word ending in the locative case [to denote a place]. Where?
In the words *yatra*,

The exception [to the previous rule] is as follows: here, the suffix *at* is substituted for *kim* [when followed by *tra*]. (Pāṇini 5.3.12)

Where? In what case? [The suffix *kvip*] is seen after other [roots] as well; Pāṇini 5.3.14.

The suffixes beginning with *tasil* are seen even after case endings other than the fifth (*pañcamī*) and seventh (*saptamī*). By virtue of the inclusion of the term "is seen" (*dṛśi*), this applies only in connection with words such as *bhavat*. Example:
*sa bhavān*.

when?

*etetau rathoḥ* | 5 | 3 | 4 | The forms *eta* and *it* replace *idam* when followed by a suffix beginning with *ra* or *tha* that belongs to the *prāgdiśīya* group. For example: *asmin kāle* becomes *etarhi*.
What [is the meaning of] *kāle*?
[It means] "in this place" (*iha deśe*).

When?
At what time? At which time?
When... then... at that time...
*etado 't* | 5 | 3 | 5 | The forms *eta* and *etad* become *eta* before suffixes beginning with *r* or *th* that belong to the *prāgdiśīya* group. For example: *etasmin kāle* becomes *etarhi*.

The suffix *thāl* occurs after words expressing a manner (*prakāra*). [Pāṇini 5.3.23] The suffix *thāl* occurs after words such as *kim* when they function to express a manner. In that manner: *tathā*.
*idam-asthamuḥ* | Pāṇini 5.3.24. This is an exception to the suffix *thāl*.
It should also be stated that this applies to *etad* as well.
In this manner, or thus: *anena* or *etena*. By what manner? *kimaśca* (Pāṇini 5.3.25). In what manner? *katham*.
Thus end the *prāgdiśīya* suffixes.
(403) *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* | P. 5.3.55. These two [suffixes, *tamap* and *iṣṭhan*], occur in their own sense (*svārthe*) when [a word] denotes a meaning characterized by excellence (*atiśaya*).
Among these, this one is exceedingly wealthy: *āḍhyatamaḥ*.
[Exceedingly light: *laghutamaḥ*, *laghiṣṭhaḥ*.

And [the suffix] *tiṅ*. (Pāṇini 5.3.56) When excellence is to be expressed, *tamap* shall be added after a word ending in a verbal suffix (*tiṅanta*). *Tarap* and *tamap* are designated as *gha*. (Pāṇini 1.1.22)

*Kim-ettiṅ-avyaya-ghād ām vā dravya-prakarṣe* | 5 | 4 | 11 | The suffix *ām* may optionally follow a word ending in *kim*, a word ending in *e*, a verbal suffix (*tiṅ*), or an indeclinable (*avyaya*) that ends in a *ghat* (a consonant other than *h* and a nasal), provided it does not denote the excellence of a substance (*dravya*). Example:
*kiṃtamām*.

The superlative suffixes -tamap and -tamām [are used]; [the suffix] -tamām [is used for the highest degree] when referring to height; however, when referring to the excellence of a substance, [the suffix] -tama is used.
The *uccaistama* tree.
(404) *tarap* and *īyasun* [are added] when two [things] or a word signifying a comparative division (*vibhajya*) is the *upapada*. Pāṇini 5.3.59:
These two suffixes occur after a word ending in a nominal or verbal suffix when there is an excellence of one out of two, or when there is a word signifying a comparative division as the *upapada*.
This is an exception to the two preceding rules.
This [suffix] is more light than those two; it is "lighter" (laghutara) or "lightest" (ladhīyas).
The people of the North are more proficient than those of the East; they are more skillful. [In the sense of] "praiseworthy," the substitute *śra* is applied [to the word *praśasya*]. Pāṇini 5.3.60.
Before the suffixes *iṣṭha* and *īyas*,
a monosyllabic base remains in its original form (*prakṛti*). That is, before *iṣṭha* and so forth, a monosyllabic base shall remain as it is.
The word *śreṣṭha* becomes *śreyas*, and [the word *jyeṣṭha*] becomes *jya*. 5.3.61.
In place of *praśasya* (most excellent), there is the substitution of *jya* before the suffixes *iṣṭhan* and *īyasun*. Thus: *jyeṣṭhaḥ*.
[The rule] *jyādādīyasaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.160) [states: In place of *jya*, there is the substitution of *ā* before the suffix *īyasun*.
[The substitute] takes the place of that which follows.
*Jyāyān*.
(405) *Bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.158): [In the formation of the comparative suffix], there is elision of *bahu*, and *bahu* is replaced by *bhū*.

There is elision of the suffixes *iyas* and *iṣṭha* when they follow *bahu*; furthermore, *bahu* undergoes the substitution of *bhū*. [The suffix] *yiṭ* is also added to *iṣṭha*. (Pāṇini 6.4.159) *Example:* *bhūmā* (abundance).
[Rule: *iṣṭhasya yiṭ ca* (6.4.159).
There shall be elision of the suffix *iṣṭha* after the word *bahu*, and the augment *yiṭ* shall also be applied. [Thus:
*bhūyiṣṭhaḥ*. [Furthermore: There is elision of the suffixes *vin* and *matup*. (Pāṇini 5.3.65)
Before the suffixes *iṣṭhan* and *īyasun*: one who is most garlanded is *srajiṣṭhaḥ*.
More garlanded;
possessing skin in an exceeding degree; most possessed of skin.
*tvacīyān* | The suffixes *kalpa*, *deśya*, and *deśīya* are used in the sense of "not quite complete" (*īṣadasamāpti*).
[Pāṇini 5.3.67] *īṣadūna* (slightly less) *vidvān* (learned).
One who is almost a scholar; one who resembles a scholar;
one who is nearly a scholar.
[The suffix] *kalpa* is added [after a word ending in a case-suffix].

(406) *Vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*: The suffix *bahuc* is optionally added after a word ending in a case-suffix, and it is placed before [the base]. Example: *īṣadūnaḥ paṭuḥ* ("slightly less than clever").
*bahupaṭuḥ* (very clever); *paṭukalpaḥ* (somewhat clever).
Why [is it] *sup*? [To exclude cases where the suffix is not *sup*.]
He cooks for a kalpa (*pacati-kalpam*).
From this point until before *prāgivāt* (Pāṇini 5.3.70), there is the governing rule for the suffix *ka*.
The section beginning with *ive pratikṛtau* (Pāṇini 5.3.96) precedes this.
The suffix *akac* is added before the final vowel (*ṭi*) of indeclinables and pronouns. (Pāṇini 5.3.71) This is an exception to [the suffix] *kā*.
It is used when something is unknown. (Pāṇini 5.3.73)
Whose horse is this, Aśvaka? [He says: "Loudly!
"Softly!"
With all [suffixes], when expressing contempt: 5.3.74. A contemptible horse is *aśvakaḥ*.
The suffixes *ḍatarac* and *ḍatamac* are applied after the words *kim*, *yat*, and *tat* when there is a selection from among two or many [respectively]. (Pāṇini 5.3.92) Example:
"Which of these two is a Vaiṣṇava? (*anayoḥ kataro vaiṣṇavaḥ*). [Similarly: *yataraḥ*.
Thereafter: "The suffix *ḍatama* is used after many [words] when there is an inquiry regarding a genus (*jāti*). (Pāṇini 5.3.93).
The phrase "when there is an inquiry regarding a genus" has been rejected in the original source (*ākara*).
Which one among you is Kaṭha? Which one? Which one?
The mention of "vā" is for the sake of [the forms] *akac* and so forth:
*yakaḥ*, *sakaḥ*.
Thus end the suffixes treated as *prāgivīya*.
In the sense of "a likeness of," [the suffix] *kan* shall be applied. A likeness of a horse (*aśvaka*).
Aśvakaḥ:
the suffix *kan* is added to all nominal stems (*prātipadika*) in the sense of the base itself; thus, *aśvakaḥ*.
(408) *tat-prakṛta-vacane mayaṭ* | 5 | 4 | 21 | "Prakṛta" means that which is presented as being abundant; its "vacana" is the expression or representation thereof.
The suffix *lyuṭ* is used here in the sense of either an abstract action (*bhāva*) or a locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
In the first [case], the food under discussion consists of cooked grain;
in the second, however, it consists of cakes.
A sacrifice consists of food;
a festival consists of cakes.
[The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after words such as *prājña*. (Pāṇini 5.4.21–23)
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied. Thus, from *prājña* comes *prājñaḥ*; from *daivata* comes *daivataḥ*.
The suffix *śas* is optionally added after a word denoting a case-relation (*kāraka*) when it signifies "much" or "little.
(Pāṇini 5.4.42) He gives much: *bahuśaḥ*. He gives little: *alpaśaḥ*.
(409) An addition [to the rule] is made for the suffix *tas* after words beginning with *ādi*:
*ādau* becomes *āditaḥ*;
likewise *madhyataḥ*.
From behind; from the back; from the side.
This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open-ended class). [Examples include: *svareṇa*, *svarataḥ*, *varṇataḥ*.

The suffix *cvi* is applied after a word denoting a material cause (*prakṛti*) when it is joined with the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, or *as*, provided that the agent is one who becomes something else (*saṃpadyakartṛ*).
It should be stated that this occurs when there is "the becoming of what was not previously so" (*abhūtatadbhāva*).

When the material cause attains the nature of a modification (*vikārātmatā*), the suffix *cvi* may optionally be applied in its own sense (*svārthe*) after a word denoting the modification, provided it is joined with *karoti* and the other roots.

*asya cvau* | 7 | 4 | 32 | The substitute *ī* shall take the place of an *a*-vowel before the suffix *cv-* [when it denotes becoming or making something what it was not]. That which was not black becomes black; one makes it so: *kṛṣṇīkaroti*.
It becomes *brahmībhavati*.
It would be *gaṅgīsyāt*.
It should be stated that there is no substitution of *ī* for *u* in an indeclinable before the suffix *cv-* [in the sense of "becoming"].
The day became a fault;
the night became day.
[The suffix] *sāti* is optionally used when expressing totality. 5.4.52.
In this context, there may be *sāti* in the sense of totality. [By the rule] *sātpadādyoḥ* (8.3.111),
the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* does not occur.
He curdles the curds.
The entire sacrificial implement becomes fire—it is reduced to fire. [The suffix *śas* is applied] after a word ending in *cv-* as well. 7.4.26.
It would be long [in form]. *agnībhavati*.
[The suffix] *ḍāc* is added after an unmanifested imitation sound (*avyaktānukaraṇa*) consisting of two or more syllables, provided it does not end in *iti*. (Pāṇini 5.4.57)
(411) It must consist of at least two syllables, but not fewer than that;
that is, as many as there may be. From such a stem consisting of [at least] two syllables, the suffix *ḍāc* shall be applied when used in conjunction with the verbs *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as*.
In the case of *ḍāc*, there is generally reduplication; that is, when *ḍāc* is intended to be applied, reduplication occurs.
It should be stated that this is obligatory when followed by an *āmreḍita*.
When an *āmreḍita* follows *ḍāc*, the single substitute form (*pararūpa*) shall take the place of both the preceding and following phonemes.
Thus, between the letter *t* and the letter *p*, the letter *p* [is substituted]. As in: *paṭapaṭā karoti*.
Why [does the rule apply] only to the imitation of indistinct sounds?
One makes a stone.
Why [is it not so] after a word ending in two consonants followed by *r*?
One makes a sound (*śrat*).
What is the purpose of [the condition] "avare"?
[The answer is: It applies to the sound *kharaṭakharaṭā*.

He makes a *paṭiti* sound.
Thus end the secondary suffixes (*taddhita*).

*ajādyataṣṭāp* | 4 | 1 | 4 | When femininity—which is to be expressed—is denoted by [words] beginning with *aja-* or by those ending in short *a*, the suffix *ṭāp* shall be applied. Example:
*ajā*.
She-goat; mare; sparrow.
Mouse; young one; child.
Hoḍā, Mandā, Vilātā.
Medhā,
and so forth;
Gaṅgā.

Nadī,

Śāktīkī, Āḍhyakaraṇī, Taruṇī.

nartakī (female dancer), gaurī (the goddess Gaurī), anaḍuhī (cow).
*anaḍvāhī*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class). [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after a word ending in *an*, provided it denotes the first stage of life. Pāṇini 4.1.20.

*tryanīkā*.

[Sūtra 4.1.39: After a word denoting a color (*varṇa*) which ends in an unaccented vowel (*anudātta*), has *t* as its penultimate letter (*topadha*), and is not a subordinate member (*anupasarjana*), the suffix *ṅīp* is optionally applied, and the *t* is replaced by *n*.

*mṛdvī* (feminine),
*mṛduḥ* (masculine/neuter).

the wife of a cowherd (*gopa*) is a *gopī*.
Not after *pālaka* when it means "beloved":

Before the suffix *āp*, when it is not preceded by a *sup* case ending, there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel *a* that precedes the letter *k* situated within a suffix. For example:

Karika: What follows from this?
A boat.
What is the purpose of [specifying] "standing after an affix" (*pratyayasthāt*)? [Consider:

The city has many wandering mendicants.
